subject: Data residency & redaction options for EU insurer pilot
messages:
From: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@novatek-insurance.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Novatek Compliance Team <compliance@novatek-ins.com>, David Lowe <david@compliancerx.io>
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask — residency & scrub options for EU customer data

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team asked for a concise options list for the EU pilot (GDPR + local regulator concerns). Two quick asks: 1) what residency controls can you offer for PII/PHI (customer names, policy numbers, claims narratives) so data never leaves EU regions; and 2) for short-lived model artifacts (KV cache, intermediate logs) what retention and redaction options exist — we need to demonstrate a plan to the regulator.

We also have a narrow use case: real-time claims triage where transcripts may contain PHI. We need a realistic recommendation (and a conservative default) for retention limits and automated redaction approaches you support.

Can you provide the options and highlight trade-offs (latency, cost, forensic ability)? Attaching our pilot scope.

Appreciate it,
Julie
Senior Product, Novatek Insurance

Attachments: Novatek_Scope.pdf (doc stub)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@novatek-insurance.com>
Cc: Novatek Compliance Team <compliance@novatek-ins.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — residency & scrub options for EU customer data

Julie — thanks for the clear brief and the scope doc. High level summary up front, then specific options below. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the team through trade-offs.

Quick summary (conservative default):
- Residency: We can provision tenant-scoped workloads in EU regions only (data plane + KV cache pinned to region). Default for pilot: EU-only processing and storage.
- Retention (conservative default): 30-day short-term cache for operational debugging + 90-day retained artifacts for audit with encrypted storage; option to reduce to 0–7 days for KV caches on demand.
- Redaction: Two-tier approach — (A) pre-ingest deterministic PII/PHI redaction via regex + NER-based classifier (edge) and (B) post-hoc field scrubbing and reversible pseudonymization for permitted forensic needs.

Options and trade-offs:
1) Full EU-only residency (recommended for pilot)
   - What: Data plane, model serving, KV caches, and logs remain in identified EU region(s).
   - Pros: Strongest regulatory posture, simplest contractual language.
   - Cons: Slightly higher latency for EU customers only if we route strictly regionally; higher cost for dedicated EU capacity.

2) Hybrid routing with EU warm fallback
   - What: Primary EU hosts; when capacity is constrained, fallback to compatible model variants in nearby regions under contractual controls.
   - Pros: better availability; lower provisioning costs.
   - Cons: Requires fallback consent in contract; more complex audit trail.

3) Retention windows (configurable per route)
   - Short-term operational cache: default 30 days (can set 0–7 days) — used for model KV caching to speed generation.
   - Audit traces (sanitized): default 90 days — low-sensitivity traces kept for incident investigation; can be shortened or disabled.

4) Redaction & pseudonymization modes
   - Deterministic masking: remove or hash fixed fields (policy numbers, SSNs) before ingest — near-zero impact on latency.
   - NER-based entity scrub: ML classifier to find names, dates, addresses — higher compute, some false positives; we recommend human review for edge cases.
   - Reversible pseudonymization: encrypt identifiers with customer-specific keys (KMS) so Novatek can re-identify records if necessary (adds complexity for key management).

5) Forensics & compliance evidence
   - We can produce auditors’ export (manifest + redaction matrix) showing which artifacts were kept and why; exports are region-scoped and signed.

Next steps proposed: 1) confirm conservative defaults (I suggest EU-only + 30d cache + 90d sanitized traces + deterministic masking), 2) pick whether reversible pseudonymization is required, 3) sign a pilot addendum and we’ll stand up an EU tenant.

Looping Naomi and Rafa for privacy/legal nuances and PrIyom for the engineering implementation notes.

Best,
Aisha
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@novatek-insurance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — residency & scrub options for EU customer data

Julie / team — quick privacy notes to accompany Aisha’s options:

- For PHI in EU jurisdiction, assume heightened regulator scrutiny and prefer the most conservative approach where operationally feasible (EU-only processing + default deterministic masking).
- Deterministic masking rules: policy numbers, national identifiers, credit card numbers — strip/replace with stable hash. Keep a mapping only if reversible pseudonymization is explicitly contractually permitted and keys are customer-managed.
- NER scrub: good for free text (claims narratives) but tune thresholds aggressively for recall over precision if the regulator prefers not retaining PHI. That means more false positives (extra manual review cost).
- Retention floors: we recommend a policy that explicitly states allowed minimum retention for operational caches (e.g., 0–7 days permitted) and retention for audit traces (e.g., 30–90 days) — but make the lower bound configurable for Novatek’s compliance team to accept.

I’m attaching a short redaction matrix (redaction_matrix.xlsx) showing field families, recommended default action (mask, pseudonymize, purge), and rationale.

-Naomi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redaction_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@novatek-insurance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — residency & scrub options for EU customer data

Julie — some implementation specifics and trade-off notes from engineering:

1) Tenant-scoping + regional pinning
   - We will provision an EU tenant with isolated namespaces and ensure the serving runtime, cache layers (KV), and artifact stores are in EU regions. This is standard for pilots.

2) Cache retention knob
   - Expose retention as a per-route config (default 30d); we can add a hardened mode that sets KV cache TTL to 0 (no caching) for strict compliance testing. Note: disabling cache increases token cost and latency (median +12–40ms depending on model).

3) Pre-ingest scrub pipeline (recommended default)
   - Lightweight regex filters for well-structured PII (policy numbers, policy-holder IDs).
   - Fast NER pass (on-edge) with conservative thresholds to remove likely PHI; flagged snippets can flow to a quarantine bucket (EU-only) for optional manual review.

4) Reversible pseudonymization & keying
   - We support customer-supplied KMS keys (recommended). Reversible mapping stored encrypted and only accessible to customer-managed KMS for re-identification. Adds ~5–10% overhead to storage ops but preserves forensic capability.

5) Auditability
   - Every retention/redaction action logged to an immutable audit stream (WORM-enabled) in EU; we can produce per-record manifests for auditors. These logs can either be retained by Redwood for the agreed window or pushed to Novatek’s S3/GCS replica.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for ops that shows the config toggles (EU-only, cache TTL, pseudonymize on/off, NER threshold) and sample curl commands to configure routes.

-Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_requirements.docx (doc stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@novatek-insurance.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — residency & scrub options for EU customer data

Julie — legal confirmation on the contract side to unblock pilot:

1) Residency & fallback: we will include a pilot addendum that states primary EU-only processing. Any cross-region fallback requires explicit written consent (we can include allowed fallback regions in an appendix).

2) Retention commitments: propose we commit to the conservative defaults Aisha suggested in the SOW (30d cache; 90d sanitized traces) with a configurable retention box for Novatek to select shorter windows.

3) Pseudonymization clause: reversible pseudonymization will only be permitted if Novatek supplies and controls the KMS keys; we will not retain re-identification ability without explicit contract terms.

4) Audit evidence: Redwood will provide signed manifests and optional log exports. Any long-term evidence storage beyond the SOW window will require an addendum.

If this matches Novatek’s needs we can produce a redline for the pilot addendum this week. Happy to sync for 30 minutes to finalize.

-Rafael
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
